The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the Death of one Muniyaiah in a road traffic accident dated 19.08.2022.

2. The case of the Petitioners in brief is that:
On 19.08.2022 at about 1.30 am the deceased Muniyaiah and son Krishna were coming from Mandya Food Office after enquiring about the Ration Card.

When they were sitting near Auto Stand, Holalu Circle, Nagamangala Road, a Tractor bearing No.KA17TA7028 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life and dashed to Muniyaiah.
Due to said accident he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. The petitioners further averred that, immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Govt. Hospital at Mandya for treatment and spent more than a sum of MFCSCCH-25 Rs.5,000/
towards hospitalization medicines and nourishment, finally same day deceased Muniyaiah died at MMIS & Govt. Hospital, Mandya, wherein post mortem examination was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies, by spending more than Rs.1,80,000/. Due to the sudden and sad demise of the deceased in the tragic accident, the petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings.
4.

The petitioners further stated that, petitioners being the wife and children of the deceased Muniyaiah were maintained by him as elderly male member/Kartha of the family, but have lost their loving and care taking person.
The deceased was a Farmer and earning more than Rs.30,000/ per month and contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners life has become dark, miserable and depressed and they are put to great financial hardship.
MFCSCCH-25 5.
The Jurisdictional Mandya Traffic Police registered case in Cr.No.62/2022 against the driver of Tractor No.KA 17TA7028.

The respondents being the Insurer and the RC owner of the offending Muniyamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122352592/
3 vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text: Hence, this petition.
6. In response to the service of notice, the Respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.2 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

7. The objections of the respondent No.1:
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle and liability to indemnify the 2nd respondent is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
There is noncompliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the vehicle was no way related in the alleged accident as MFCSCCH-25 on the date of accident.
The Driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income, avocation, dependency of the petitioners and the manner of accident.
It has contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Muniyaiah.?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Muniyaiah had died due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 19.08.2022 at about 1.30am near Auto Stand, Holalu Circle, Nagamangala Road, Mandya City, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA17TA 7028 as alleged?
3 . Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What Order or Award?
MFCSCCH-25 9.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined Petitioner No.6 - Sri.Krishna - Son of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.
The Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.

10. Heard both the Counsels and perused the materials on record.
11.

My finding to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1 : Partly in the affirmative Issue Nos.2 &
3 : In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:

sentences.text: Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner Nos.2 to 7 are the daughters and son of the deceased - Muniyaiah.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 6th Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 MFCSCCH-25 has specifically spoken about this relationship in his chief examination.

Apart from that,
to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have produced their Notarized copies of Aadhar Cards as per Ex.P.11.
In Ex.P.11 - Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.1, her husband's name is mentioned as Muniyaiah and in the Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.6, his father's name is mentioned as Muniyaiah.

In the Aadhar Cards of the petitioner Nos.2 to 5 and 7, their husband's names are mentioned as Late Kashi,
Shashikumar, Paschima, Manikkam and Murugavelu respectively.
No other document is produced to show the relationship of petitioner Nos.2 to 5 & 7 to the deceased.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.

As such,
there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.
Under such circumstances, MFCSCCH-25 relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 & 6 are the Wife and son of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held partly in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:

The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tractor have examined Petitioner No.6 as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.10.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
On the other side, the Respondents have denied the involvement and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. The documents produced by the Petitioners such as the FIR in Cr.No.62/2022 of Mandya Traffic Police with Complaint registered on 19.08.2022, chargesheet, spot mahazar, Inquest mahazar, PM report, MLC register extract MFCSCCH-25 and MVA report as per Exs.P.1 to P.10 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.
These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.

The investigation officer in crime No.62/2022 of Mandya Traffic Police has conducted the investigation in detail and has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending Tractor bearing No.KA17TA7028 holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Tractor.
During the cross examination of PW.1 by the respondent1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
Therefore, from the evidence of PW.1 it can be gathered that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the Tractor.

sentences.text: The Inquest mahazar produced as per Ex.P.6 and PM report produced as per Ex.P.8 clearly show that 'Death is due to SHOCK & HEMORRHAGE as a result of injuries sustained and on account of such injuries has succumbed to his death.
In support of their defence the respondents did not MFCSCCH-25 examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of the offending Tractor.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and his loving father.

He has further deposed that they have spent Rs.1,50,000/ towards conveyance,
transportation of dead body and for performing the funeral ceremonies.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
Monthly income 17.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was a Farmer and earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
The Petitioners to prove the income of the deceased have not produced any documents such as RTCs, Bank Statement, details of crop MFCSCCH-25 growing etc., nor have they examined any witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
Under such circumstances, this court has to consider the income at Rs.15,000/ notionally for calculating the compensation.
Age of the deceased 18.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.11.
As per Ex.P.11, deceased birth year was 1947.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 74 years.
Therefore, his age is considered as 74 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:

As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,
appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 5.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the MFCSCCH-25 deceased has a wifepetitioner No.1, aged about 67 years and a major son - Petitioner No.6, aged about 34 years.
As above said, the deceased has married daughters also and all the children are major and settled.
Therefore, they are not considered as the dependents of the deceased.
Only petitioner No.1 is the dependent of the deceased.

19. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others (AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged about above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the Sarala Verma case, if there is a sole dependent then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.7,500/.

Therefore, the Muniyamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122352592/
6 total loss of dependency would be Rs.4,50,000/ (Rs.7,500/ X 5 x 12) = Rs.4,50,000/).

sentences.text: MFCSCCH-25 ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018)
18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text:
Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018)
18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.

With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".
20.

This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
21.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The 1st Petitioner is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 67 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is MFCSCCH-25 entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/ under the head of loss of consortium.
Similarly, the petitioner No.6 is the son of the deceased, he has lost his loving, care taking father.
Therefore, he is also entitled to Rs.44,000/, in total Rs.88,000/ is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.
iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.1,50,000/ towards funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/2 of MFCSCCH-25 his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.

As such, in total, the Petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs..5,78,000/.
LIABILITY 22.
As discussed above the respondents did not prove their defence.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer and the respondent No.2 being the Owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Though the Petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000, but Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,78,000/ along with interest @ 6%
per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,78,000/ (Rupees Five Lakhs Seventy Eight Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount from the Respondents.
The respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
MFCSCCH-25 The Respondent No.1 shall indemnify the Respondent No.2 and deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.44,000/ shall be released to the petitioner No.6 and remaining entire amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of epayment with proper identification and due acknowledgments.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
